**D0048 – "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (Apple)** — Theoretical analysis of deep linear self-distillation. Key finding: JEPA is biased toward high-influence features (large regression coefficient ρ) and suppresses noisy/low-ρ directions, increasingly so with depth; MAE instead prioritizes high-variance features. - **D0048** "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (Apple): JEPA vs MAE in deep linear networks. JEPA is biased toward high-influence features (large regression coefficient ρ) and suppresses noisy features, increasingly with depth; MAE's learning order depends only on variance λ and learns noisy, low-ρ features. Theory: 1-layer JEPA = infinite-depth MAE; JEPA critical time is ρ-sensitive (eq. 14), MAE's is not. Validated via ODE simulations and SGD on Gaussian data; on ImageNet ViT, JEPA learns low-variance features faster. Note: this is a theory/analysis paper — no F1/Precision/AUROC.

## 6. End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning — D0060 (ICML 2025)
LoRA fine-tuning (TinyLlama-1B on MathQA) improves task performance but does **not** significantly alter the backbone's Hessian structure (power-law spectrum doesn't emerge with LoRA as with full fine-tuning); for pretrained models the Hessian trace Tr(H) is a more reliable generalization indicator than sharpness. Related: D0051 uses LoRA for fine-tuning baselines; D0044 treats LoRA as conceptually equivalent to full fine-tuning.

## Cross-method comparison
- **Association > detection:** PBADet's biggest wins are in association metrics (JointAP, mMR⁻²), mirroring how LDReg's biggest gains are in representation quality (LID/rank) rather than raw accuracy.
- **Reward–diversity trade-off:** RTB (like LDReg's regularization) deliberately sacrifices peak reward for diversity/FID, whereas DDPO/DDPO-style pure reward maximization mode-collapses — a recurring theme of regularization-vs-optimization.
- **Guarantees vs empirics:** D0004 is the only method with finite-sample, anytime-valid statistical guarantees; RTB is asymptotically correct but has no error guarantees — matching the safety layer's requirement.
- **Spectral health predicts training:** D0069 (NSE) and D0060 (power-law Hessian/KS distance) both show that spectral properti…

**N原judge：** The generated answer captures most core results and comparisons from the gold answer, but includes a minor factual error about which foot PBADet improves and a slight overstatement on D4RL, so it is good but not perfect.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## 5. Stable time-series controller training (E/I + spectral) → **"Learning better with Dale's Law" (D0069, NeurIPS 2023)**
Directly on your E/I constraint: RNNs obeying Dale's law (Column E/I, "ColEI") train poorly, but recurrent **DANNs** match standard RNNs. Key finding: **spectral properties matter more than sign constraints** — ColEI singular-value spectra are multimodal/dispersed with a large-singular-value mode (activations/gradients get stretched), while standard RNNs/DANNs follow the Marchenko–Pastur quarter-circle law. Spectrum-transplant experiments: singular-value spectrum contributes ~1.5–2% test error vs ~0.7–1% for sign constraints. **Normalized SVD entropy** quantifies the pathology and anti-correlates with performance; gradient clipping helps ColEI disproportionately. (Note: no spectral-radius regularization is proposed here per se — the "stability" insight is that spectrum shape, not sign constraints, drives learning.)

## 6. Fine-tuning large backbones / End-to-end LoRA
No paper in this collection presents an "End-to-end LoRA" method per se. Closest evidence:
- **D0060** (Hessian power laws, ICML 2025): power-law Hessian spectra hold across optimizers (**SGD, Adam, AMSGrad, RAdam, Yogi, AdaBound, etc.**) and **slope magnitude ŝ correlates with sharpness and te…

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0063：PBADet introduces a one-stage, anchor-free detector for human part-body association, representing each part by a single 2D offset to its parent body center. It outperforms BPJDet on BodyHands, matches or exceeds it on COCOHumanParts, surpasses ED-Pose in part-body association, and generalizes to quadruped animal part-body association.
  - 社区 C0041 的组织线索：These three object detection papers: PBADet for human part-body association, HASSOD for class-agnostic object discovery, and MonoUNI for monocular 3D detection.


- D0006：CleanDiffuser is a modular open-source library for diffusion models in decision-making, supporting planner, policy, and data-synthesizer roles. It integrates samplers, architectures, guided sampling; ~10-line pipelines, 37 benchmarks. Findings: algorithm/architecture dominate model size, DQL strong, sampling degradation possible.
  - 社区 C0036 的组织线索：Covers diffusion models in decision-making: a modular library for planners/policies/data synthesis, and an amortized posterior-sampling objective for reward-guided generation.


这些概览能够帮助找到方法和实验方向，但通常没有同一表中的 baseline/数据集/指标/配置四元组。数值或胜负变化应归到实际表格证据和答案取舍，不能仅归到社区名字。


**背景负担的具体例子：** C0019「Theoretical Machine Learning and Optimization」有 5 篇成员、0 篇G成员；其overview为“Theoretical work on machine learning and algorithms: nonsmooth optimization, private optimization, hyperparameter search, parameter partitioning, and similarity learning.”。例如 D0008《When Does Automatic Differentiation Compute a Clarke Subgradient for ReLU/Maxpool Networks?》, D0042《Improved Private Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization》 仅以overview出现。它们可能回应附加要求，不能一律叫噪声；但若无进一步原文/答案使用证据，本次只能确认它们占用了上下文，不能确认带来收益。

1. **PBADet (ICLR 2024)** — *One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association* (D0063). A one-stage, anchor-free detector that links human parts (hands, face, feet) to parent bodies via a single part-to-body center offset; evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, and animal datasets.

**PBADet (D0063).** The only work reporting Precision/Recall/F1, on COCO. Against ED-Pose on COCO val (left/right hand, left/right foot): **F1 48.52 vs 31.51, Precision 39.41 vs 24.09, Recall 63.09 vs 45.51** — clearly better part-body association. On COCO-HumanParts it reaches **AP 43.0/41.8 (YOLOv5l6) and 42.7/41.5 (YOLOv7)**, beating BPJDet (AP ~30.8–31.8) with fewer parameters (36.9M vs 86.1M). Ablations confirm the anchor-free + part-to-body design helps: Cond. Accuracy 92.62, JointAP 85.98 (vs anchor-based 92.31/85.28).

**C原judge：** The answer covers all five papers and several comparisons, but contains key inaccuracies—most notably claiming PBADet beats BPJDet on COCO-HumanParts with AP ~30.8–31.8, whereas the gold standard reports BPJDet's AP as 43.6/43.3—so it is only partially correct.

## 4. Anchor-free detector for part–body association — D0063 "PBADet"
- Method: one-stage anchor-free detector with a single part-to-body center offset (2D vector), guaranteeing one-to-one part→body correspondence regardless of part count/visibility.
- Results:
  - BodyHands (YOLOv7): HandAP 89.1, Conditional Accuracy 92.62, JointAP 85.98; ablations show the association head is decisive (JointAP 78.07→85.98), with multi-scale and task-alignment helping.
  - vs. ED-Pose on COCO val (Precision/Recall/F1): all parts F1 48.52 vs. 31.51, Precision 39.41 vs. 24.09, Recall 63.09 vs. 45.51 — this is the F1/Precision evidence on COCO.
  - COCO-HumanParts: AP 42.7/41.5 (YOLOv7) and 43.0/41.8 (YOLOv5l6); CrowdHuman face-body MR-2 36.5/44.7, body AP 91.6.
  - Anchor-free beats anchor-based (89.1 vs. 88.4 HandAP) and part-to-body beats body-to-part (BPJDet: 85.3/86.80/78.13 vs. 89.1/92.62/85.98).
- Compatibility: backbones are YOLO (CNN), not ResNet-50; it outperforms a transformer (Swin-L ED-Pose) baseline. Uses classification + box-regression (DFL) losses.

## Comparative summary
- The five documents collectively cover your five topics, but the strongest experimental match is D0059 (lossless accuracy with ~43–58% memory savings) and D0063 (clear COCO F1/Precision and AP wins over ED-Pose/BP…

Are there papers that bring together anchor-free part–body detection, offline combinatorial bandits, JEPA-style self-supervised learning, memory-efficient optimizers, and spectral perspectives on biologically constrained RNNs—using CE/MSE, cosine similarity, and LoRA fine-tuning?Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

## 2. Implicit bias of JEPA vs. pixel-space reconstruction — D0048
**"JEPA and MAE Feature Learning Dynamics: High-Dimensional Linear Models and Critical Times"** (Apple)
- Shows JEPA (joint-embedding self-distillation) is biased toward **high-influence features** (large regression coefficient ρ), avoiding noisy, high-variance features, while MAE (pixel-space reconstruction) greedily learns high-covariance features even if noisy/uninformative.
- **Results:** derived ODEs show the only JEPA/MAE difference is an exponent; JEPA critical time is ρ-sensitive (depth-dependent), MAE's is λ-(variance-)dependent; 1-layer JEPA = infinite-depth MAE; deeper encoders increasingly suppress noisy directions; verified by ODE simulations, SGD on Gaussian data, and ImageNet ViT experiments (JEPA learns low-variance features faster). Feature quality is tracked via regression-coefficient-type metrics (the style of representation check you mention), not cosine similarity.

## 5. Anchor-free one-stage part–whole association detector — D0063
**"PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association"** (ICLR 2024)
- One-stage, anchor-free, **no attention-heavy heads** — three lightweight 3-layer conv branches (box/class/association) on multi-scale features, with a single part-to-body center offset and TOOD…

**N原judge：** The generated answer accurately captures the core findings, metrics, and comparisons for all five papers, consistent with the gold answer and adding context without contradictions.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

1. **Spectral analyses of EI-constrained RNNs (Dale's law)** — *Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (D0069, NeurIPS 2023). ColEI vs. DANN vs. standard RNNs.
2. **JEPA self-distillation vs. pixel reconstruction implicit bias** — *How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks* (D0048).
3. **Token-level decoding signatures for CoT** — *TokenSignature: Predicting Chain-of-Thought Gains with Token Decoding Feature in LLMs* (D0034, ICML 2025).
4. **Memory-lean 4-bit optimizers** — *Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States* (D0059, NeurIPS 2023).
5. **Anchor-free part–body association detector** — *PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association* (D0063, ICLR 2024).

**D0048 (representation bias).** Both JEPA and MAE show greedy step-wise feature learning, but under distributions where variance λ and regression coefficient ρ conflict, MAE keeps learning order by λ while JEPA *inverts* it, learning high-influence (high-ρ) features first. JEPA suppresses noisy, low-ρ directions, with suppression growing with depth; a 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. This explains why JEPA avoids noisy pixel-level features.

**C原judge：** The generated answer is largely accurate and detailed, matching most of the gold results across all five papers, but it has minor factual imprecisions—e.g., incorrectly stating that PBADet has the lowest mMR−2 for the right foot and claiming no cosine-similarity/CCA representation comparisons are found when the JEPA paper reports mean CCA comparisons.

## (b) Spectral analyses of optimizers and EI constraints (D0060, D0069)
- D0060 (Hessian spectra): trained networks (LeNet/ResNet, MNIST/CIFAR, GPT2 LLMs) show power-law Hessian spectra that hold across **SGD, Vanilla SGD, Adam, AMSGrad, AdaBound, Yogi, RAdam, Adai, PNM, Lookahead, DiffGrad**—as long as the optimizer trains well; **AdamW** is used for the LLM experiments. The fitted slope ŝ correlates with sharpness and generalization (Pearson 0.853 on MNIST test error). Large batch sizes (B>640–768) break the power law and harm generalization.
- D0069 (Dale's Law / EI constraints): excitatory/inhibitory (ColEI) RNNs learn worse because their singular-value spectra are multimodal/dispersed, not mainly because of sign constraints; **spectral properties matter more than sign constraints** (transplant experiments, sequential MNIST). Normalized SVD entropy predicts performance.
- **Limitation:** neither paper explicitly contrasts CE vs MSE objectives; the CE-vs-MSE impact on learning is **not established** in these documents (they use softmax/classification losses and MSE-style regression only indirectly).

**(b) Spectral analyses (D0069, D0060, D0085)**
- D0069 (EI/Dale’s-Law RNNs): the singular-value spectrum of ColEI networks (multimodal/dispersed) is more impactful than the sign (excitatory/inhibitory) constraint itself. Normalised SVD entropy (NSE) at initialization anti-correlates with final test error on sequential MNIST, object recognition, and language modeling; smaller networks with balanced E/I (high NSE) beat larger ones with skewed ratios.
- D0060 (Hessian spectra): the power-law Hessian spectrum holds across optimizers (SGD, Vanilla SGD, Adam, AMSGrad, AdaBound, RAdam, Yogi, Adai, PNM, Lookahead, DiffGrad). The fitted slope magnitude ŝ is an indicator of sharpness and a predictor of test error (Pearson ≈0.853 on MNIST, 0.72 on CIFAR-10). It also notes SGD performs worse than Adam on Transformers when Hessian spectra show blockwise heterogeneity.
- D0085 (loss choice): classification losses with exponential tails (e.g., CE) yield an initialization-independent margin-maximizing implicit bias, whereas regression (MSE) implicit bias is decisively affected by initialization scale — small initialization biases toward low-rank/minimal-norm solutions but with longer training.

## Comparative analysis of the experimental results

## 4. Privacy-preserving synthetic tabular + time-series — Synthcity (D0074)
Benchmark framework covering static, regular/irregular time-series, and censored-survival data, with generators from GAN (CTGAN, TimeGAN, DPGAN, PATEGAN), VAE (TVAE, TimeVAE), flow (FourierFlow), diffusion (TabDDPM), and tree-based (ARF) families, and metrics for fidelity, **utility (downstream linear/MLP/XGBoost classifiers)**, fairness (Demographic Parity, Conditional Fairness, minority-group AUROC), and privacy (k-anonymity, l-diversity, delta-presence, DOMIAS, DP/threat models).
- Static tabular (quality↑/detection↓): TVAE 0.5487/0.7389, ARF 0.5475/0.6721, CTGAN 0.5475/0.7758, TabDDPM 0.5436/0.7074, GOGGLE 0.4054/0.9261 — tree-based ARF is a strong competitor to deep models.
- Fairness/augmentation (SIVEP-Gripe minority mortality AUROC): augmentation consistently helps — TabDDPM best (0.7241 NN / 0.7786 XGB) > RadialGAN (0.7137/0.7627) > CTGAN (0.6477/0.7507) > TVAE (0.3623/0.7794) vs baseline (0.3244/0.7327).

**Bottom line:** PBADet gives the real-time detector; DoReMi the data-mix speedup; JEPA (latent prediction, optionally +LDReg) the noise-avoiding SSL objective; Synthcity the synthetic-data generators/checks; and the Dale's-Law paper explains the spectral cause of EI-RNN training failure (chec…

## 4. Privacy-preserving synthetic tabular/time-series data (D0074 Synthcity)
Benchmark framework covering static + time-series (TimeGAN/TimeVAE/FourierFlow/ProbabilisticAR), DP and threat-model privacy, fairness, and downstream utility:
- **Static tabular quality/detection (18 OpenML sets):** ARF 0.5475/0.6721, TVAE 0.5487/0.7389, CTGAN 0.5475/0.7758, TabDDPM 0.5436/0.7074, GOGGLE 0.4054/0.9261. Tree-based ARF is a strong competitor to deep generators.
- **Fairness/augmentation (SIVEP-Gripe minority-group mortality AUROC):** TabDDPM best (0.7241 NN / 0.7786 XGB), then RadialGAN (0.7137/0.7627), CTGAN (0.6477/0.7507), TVAE (0.3623/0.7794), all above baseline (0.3244/0.7327) — augmentation consistently helps minority groups.

## Cross-cutting analysis
- **Both vision-detection and LM-data works show "architecture/objective choice beats capacity":** PBADet wins with a smaller model (36.9M vs 86.1M BPJDet), and DoReMi transfers gains from a 280M proxy to a 30× larger model with only weight changes.
- **"What you optimize determines what you learn" is the common thread:** JEPA's latent objective steers to high-influence features (vs MAE's variance capture), and ColEI RNNs fail due to spectral geometry of the initial weights, not the biological constraint itself — mirroring DoReMi's i…

## 2. JEPA implicit bias (D0048, NeurIPS 2024) + contrastive cosine geometry (D0014)
- **D0048** ("How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features") analyzes joint-embedding predictive objectives learning in latent space vs. MAE input-space reconstruction, using **mean-squared (L2) objectives** in deep linear networks. Finding: JEPA is biased toward "influential" (high-regression-coefficient) features while MAE prioritizes high-variance features; this bias appears only with deep encoders. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive, MAE's is not; JEPA learns low-variance ("slow") features faster (empirically, ImageNet ViT).
- **D0014** ("On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning") covers the **angular/cosine-similarity** side: full-batch optima require positive similarity = 1 and negatives = −1/(n−1); smaller mini-batches induce higher variance in negative-pair similarities, degrading representations; its proposed variance-reduction auxiliary loss improves accuracy on CIFAR and ImageNet. InfoNCE/SigLIP (softmax/cross-entropy-type) are analyzed.
- **Caveat:** no single paper in the corpus explicitly compares MSE vs. cross-entropy vs. cosine for JEPA objectives; D0048 covers MSE-based JEPA bias and D0014 covers cosine/softmax contrastive geometry separately.

## Cross-method comparis…

**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## 2. JEPA implicit bias — "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (D0048, NeurIPS 2024)
Joint-embedding predictive objectives predicting in latent space (self-distillation JEPA vs. MAE reconstruction), analyzed on deep linear networks. Both objectives share SVD dynamics, but JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive, biasing it toward "influential" (high-regression-coefficient) features — only when the encoder is deep; 1-layer JEPA ≡ infinite-depth MAE. Empirical: on ImageNet ViT, JEPA learns low-variance features faster. **Caveat:** this paper uses a mean-squared (L2) latent loss only; the requested comparison of MSE vs. cross-entropy losses and cosine/angular similarity for JEPA is **not covered** by any paper in the collection (D0014 analyzes cosine similarity of embeddings but in *contrastive* learning, validated on CIFAR/ImageNet, not JEPA) — so that aspect cannot be established from the provided context.

## Comparative analysis
- **Common theme:** all five modify training-time behavior (noise augmentation, latent-space objective, low-bit optimizer states, sign/spectral constraints, part-to-body supervision) rather than inference-time changes, targeting generalization or efficiency.
- **Benchmarks (as preferred):** COCO is used by PBADet (part-body detection) and by LDReg's fine…

**(a) NEFTune (D0001).** On AlpacaEval win rate vs ChatGPT, LLaMA-2-7B + Alpaca rises from 29.79% to 64.69% (+34.9); Evol-Instruct +9.3 (70.3→79.6), ShareGPT +7.5, OpenPlatypus +8.6, average 57.7→72.8. Gains concentrate on conversational quality; OpenLLM-Leaderboard-style tasks are unchanged — exactly your "better chat, same metrics" goal. Ablations: beats dropout (47.8) and weight decay (48.0) vs baseline 48.5 (NEFTune 61.9); gains plateau after ~3 epochs (62.55 at 3 epochs vs 58.14 at 9); freezing attention blocks removes gains; default α=15 flips <0.4% of tokens, so semantics are preserved.

## (a) Noise into embeddings for SFT chat quality
**D0001 – NEFTune: Noisy Embeddings Improve Instruction Finetuning (ICLR 2024).** Adds iid uniform noise scaled by α/√(Ld) to embeddings during finetuning. Results: LLaMA-2-7B AlpacaEval win rate 29.8→64.7% (+34.9); average +15.1% across Alpaca/Evol-Instruct/ShareGPT/OpenPlatypus; 70B Evol-Instruct 75.03→88.81% (+13.78). Crucially, OpenLLM Leaderboard (ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA) performance is **unchanged** — chat improves, factual/standard metrics don't suffer. Dropout/weight decay do **not** reproduce the gain (61.9 vs 47.8/48.0/48.5). Note: may weaken toxicity-refusal ability.

**Summary for your pipeline:** NEFTune (a) + 4-bit optimizer (b) combine cleanly with your LoRA/AdamW memory-constrained SFT and preserve OpenLLM/F1 metrics while lifting chat quality; PBADet (c) for COCO part-person association; D0048 (d) justifies JEPA-style latent prediction over pixel reconstruction; D0069 (e) explains why naive Dale's-law partitioning destabilizes learning via spectral pathology rather than sign constraints.

Here are the five papers that collectively cover the requested themes, with an analysis of their experimental results.

## (a) PBADet — One-stage anchor-free part–body association (D0063)
Evaluated on **COCOHumanParts** (66,808 train imgs), **BodyHands**, and **CrowdHuman**. On BodyHands, PBADet (YOLOv7, 36.9M params) beats BPJDet (YOLOv5m6, 41.2M): HandAP **89.1 vs 85.3**, Conditional Accuracy **92.62 vs 86.80**, JointAP **85.98 vs 78.13**; even with the same YOLOv5l6 backbone it wins (88.1/92.71/85.73). On COCOHumanParts it reaches AP .5:.95 of **42.7/41.5** (original/subordinate) with YOLOv7 and 43.0/41.8 with YOLOv5l6, on par with BPJDet and best on person/feet AP. Ablations show anchor-free > anchor-based (89.1 vs 88.4 HandAP) and part-to-body > body-to-part association (85.98 vs 78.13 JointAP).

**N原judge：** The generated answer correctly covers all five papers and most key results, but it has some imprecisions/omissions relative to the gold answer (e.g., BodyHands comparison values/baseline, memory-savings range, and missing CrowdHuman/association-mMR details).


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

Based on the document collection, I found matching papers for four of the five requested topics and the closest available match for the fifth. Here is a brief comparison of each.

## (a) Human part–body association — **PBADet** (D0063, ICLR 2024)
- **Method:** One-stage, anchor-free detection that encodes part-to-body association as a single 2D center offset, built on YOLOv5/YOLOv7 with multi-scale feature maps and a task-alignment (TOOD-style) loss.
- **Results (COCO-style human datasets):** On BodyHands it beats BPJDet (Hand AP 89.1 vs 85.3; Joint AP 85.98 vs 78.13 with YOLOv7). On COCO-HumanParts its YOLOv5l6 variant reaches 43.0/41.8 AP (original/subordinate) and 70.0/68.4 AP@0.5. On CrowdHuman face–body association it lowers MR-2 (36.5 vs BPJDet's 40.7) while keeping AP competitive. Against multi-person pose estimator ED-Pose (Swin-L) on COCO, it raises all-part F1 from 31.51 to 48.52.
- **Analysis:** Anchor-free + part-to-body formulation outperforms anchor-based body-to-part designs; ablations show the association loss, multi-scale offsets, and task alignment each contribute (full model 92.62% conditional accuracy vs 80.78% without the association loss).

**C原judge：** The generated answer accurately captures all five papers' core findings and key experimental results, aligns with the gold comparison, and adds only consistent supporting context.

**D0063 (PBADet, ICLR 2024)** — one-stage anchor-free part-to-body center-offset detector.

## Research covering your five pieces

**1. Part-body detection & association (COCO-like) — PBADet (D0063, ICLR 2024)**
One-stage anchor-free detector linking each body part (head, face, hands, feet) to its parent person via a single part-to-body center offset.
- *BodyHands:* Ours(YOLOv7) hand AP 89.1 / conditional 92.62 / joint AP 85.98 vs. BPJDet(YOLOv5l6) 85.9/86.91/84.39 and BodyHands 84.8/83.44/63.48 — wins all metrics with a smaller model.
- *COCOHumanParts:* Ours(YOLOv5l6) AP.5:.95 43.0/41.8 (orig/subordinate) vs. BPJDet 43.6/43.3, but PBADet leads AP_M (66.2 vs 63.8), AP_L (67.2 vs 61.8) and person AP (62.4 vs 61.3); lowest mMR⁻² on head/face/hands/right foot. Trained with SGD + AMP on 4×V100, 100 epochs.
- vs. pose estimation (ED-Pose/Swin-L): all-parts precision 39.41 vs 24.09, recall 63.09 vs 45.51, F1 48.52 vs 31.51. Also generalizes to quadruped part-body (AnimalPose/AP-10K).

Prefer works discussing interpretability, attention, and common evaluation protocols.Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


- D0059：Proposes 4-bit quantization of Adam/AdamW states via normalization and dynamic exponent mapping, with block-wise or rank-1 normalization for outliers. Second moment uses zero-excluding mapping and rank-1 scaling. Matches full-precision across GLUE, E2E, SQuAD, Swin, LLaMA; up to 57.7% memory savings. Provides convergence theorem for quantized SGD.
  - 社区 C0027 的组织线索：Efficient neural network optimization: online binary spiking training, quantized 4-bit optimizer states, and compressed distributed SGD, all with convergence guarantees.

**N答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## (c) "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (D0048) — JEPA implicit bias (partial match)
- Theory (deep linear self-distillation): JEPA is biased toward **high-influence features** (large regression coefficient ρ), while MAE only prioritizes high-covariance (high-variance) features. Critical-time analysis: JEPA learns features with higher ρ first, increasingly with depth (1-layer JEPA ≡ infinite-depth MAE); JEPA suppresses noisy/low-ρ, low-variance ("slow") features.
- Empirical validation: simulations on Gaussian data, and ImageNet with a **ViT encoder** showing I-JEPA learns low-variance features faster than MAE (CCA on variance-filtered subsets).
- **Gap**: no demonstrations on MNIST/CIFAR-100 or a ResNet-50 backbone appear here. The closest ResNet-50/CIFAR-100 SSL experiments are in **LDReg (D0061)**, but that paper targets local-dimensionality regularization of contrastive SSL (SimCLR/BYOL/MAE), not the JEPA predictive bias toward high-influence signals. So this sub-criterion is only partially covered.

**Not established from context**: exact SGD/AdamW usage in (b); MNIST/CIFAR-100/ResNet-50 demonstrations in (c); explicit MSE/cross-entropy losses in (a) (the text reports IoU/DFL/classification/L1 association losses instead).

**N原judge：** The generated answer accurately covers the five papers, key experimental results, and cross-method comparisons, but loses full credit due to minor inaccuracies/overstated caveats (e.g., saying CE/SGD-AdamW usage is unconfirmed in PBADet/Dale's Law, and glossing Adafactor as degrading) that slightly conflict with the gold summary.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## (c) Self-supervised joint-embedding predictive training biased to high-influence features — **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features"** (D0048)
- Analyzes JEPA (self-distillation, StopGrad) vs. MAE in deep linear networks. JEPA is biased to learn "influential" features (high regression coefficient ρ), steering away from the top-variance subspace; MAE prioritizes high-covariance/noisy features. The bias deepens with encoder depth; 1-layer JEPA ≡ infinite-depth MAE.
- **Note on demonstrations:** the paper's practical demonstration uses a ViT encoder (I-JEPA vs MAE) on ImageNet-1K (64×64), showing JEPA learns low-variance (bottom-PCA) features faster via CCA similarity. **MNIST, CIFAR-100, and ResNet-50-specific experiments are NOT present in this document** — those claims cannot be verified from the collection.

## Caveats (not established in the collection)
- **(a)** Standard "MSE/cross-entropy" losses are not explicitly reported; PBADet uses IoU/DFL/classification (task-alignment) losses, and the association loss is ℓ1-style regression.
- **(b)** The SGD vs. AdamW distinction is not discussed; spectral analysis is at initialization, with NSE as the key metric.
- **(c)** MNIST, CIFAR-100, and ResNet-50 demonstrations for the JEPA high-influence bias are not found; the only large-scale…

**C原judge：** The generated answer accurately captures the main structure and most experimental results of the gold answer, but minor imprecisions and omissions—such as slightly inconsistent BPJDet baseline numbers and missing some PBADet/CrowdHuman details—prevent a perfect score.

## 3. 4-bit optimizer states (D0059, NeurIPS 2023)
Addresses (3): memory-efficient fine-tuning with 4-bit quantized first/second moments for Adam/AdamW (framework also covers SGD/SGDM, with a convergence theorem for quantized SGDM). Uses smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, and a zero-excluding linear quantizer for the second moment, plus factorized second moment ("4-bitFactor").
**Results:** matches 32-bit AdamW across NLU (RoBERTa-L GLUE 89.1 vs 88.9), CLS (Swin-T on ImageNet-1k 80.8 vs 81.2), NLG (BLEU 67.8 vs 67.7), QA (F1 94.5 vs 94.6), MT (SacreBleu 26.28 vs 26.61); comparable on LLaMA-7B/13B/33B Alpaca fine-tuning (e.g., LLaMA-13B MMLU 47.4 vs 46.5). Saves up to 57.7% total memory (LLaMA-7B 75.4→31.9GB) vs 37.1% for 8-bit. Ablations: smaller block size improves first-moment accuracy; factorizing second moment improves accuracy and memory. **Note:** the vision benchmark is Swin-T on ImageNet; no explicit ResNet-50/CIFAR/MNIST results are reported in the retrieved content.

## Comparative analysis
- **Complementary evaluation themes:** LDReg (D0061) and 4-bit optimizers (D0059) both report ImageNet results, but for different purposes — LDReg improves SSL representation quality (higher linear-eval and detection AP), whereas the 4-bit optimizer seeks lossless accuracy (≤~0.4 …

## 3. Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States (D0059) — topic (3)
4-bit quantization of first/second moments (block-wise + rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer) for Adam/AdamW (framework also covers SGD/SGDM). **Results:** 4-bit AdamW matches or exceeds 32-bit AdamW — RoBERTa-L GLUE 89.1 vs 88.9; Swin-T ImageNet-1k 80.8 vs 81.2; GPT-2 E2E BLEU 67.8 vs 67.7; SQuAD F1 94.5 vs 94.6; WMT14 26.28 vs 26.61; LLaMA-7B MMLU 38.9 vs 38.7. Memory savings up to 57.7% (LLaMA-7B: 31.87 GB vs 75.40 GB), better than 8-bit optimizers and clearly better than Adafactor/SM3, which degrade (especially on image classification). *Note:* experiments cover Transformers (RoBERTa, GPT-2, Transformer-Base, LLaMA) and Swin-T on ImageNet; SGD and ResNet-50 are supported in the framework but not the reported benchmark set.

## Cross-paper analysis
- **Datasets:** ImageNet (LDReg, 4-bit Swin-T), COCO/COCOHumanParts (LDReg fine-tuning, PBADet), CIFAR-10/100 and MNIST (LDReg transfer; Dale's Law sequential MNIST) — matching your criteria; D0048 is primarily theory/simulations with ImageNet ViT support.

## Relevant Works and Experimental Comparisons

### 2. Restoration networks as implicit priors — **DRP (D0081)**
Generalizes plug-and-play denoiser priors to *any* pre-trained restoration network (SwinIR SR, USRNet deblurring) for other inverse problems (deblurring, SISR). **Results (deblurring, PSNR/LPIPS):** DRP with SR prior beats PnP-ADMM, IRCNN+, DPIR on Set3c (30.69/0.056 vs DPIR 29.53/0.110), Set5 (32.79/0.109), CBSD68 (29.10/0.246). **Results (SISR):** DRP(Deblur) outperforms DPIR and matches DRP(SR), e.g., Set3c 2×: 29.13 vs 28.18 (DPIR); direct use of a mismatched deblurring prior fails without DRP. Theoretical: converges to a stationary point; assumes MMSE restoration, but L1/SSIM-trained priors still work. This directly addresses your blurry-camera deblurring/SR need.

**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## 2. 复原网络作为隐式先验（去模糊/SR）：DRP (D0081)
- **方法**：Deep Restoration Prior——把预训练复原网络（SwinIR SR、USRNet 去模糊）当作隐式先验，迭代交替“先验步 + 数据保真近端步”，比传统 PnP（仅去噪器先验）更通用；有收敛到复合目标函数驻点的理论（MMSE 假设）。
- **去模糊结果**（Set3c 等，PSNR/LPIPS）：DRP 30.69/0.056 优于 DPIR 29.53/0.110、PnP-ADMM 29.11/0.099、IRCNN+ 28.14/0.086。
- **SISR（2×/3×，Set3c/Set5/CBSD68/McMaster）**：DRP(SR) 与 DRP(去模糊先验) 全面达到最佳/次佳，例如 2× Set3c：DRP(Deblur) 29.13/0.921/0.082 vs DPIR 28.18/0.908/0.137。直接用去模糊网络做 SR 不 work，但作为 DRP 先验即可工作——**正好应对你“相机偶尔模糊 + 低分辨率”的需求**。

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0003：Video pretraining for RL under exogenous noise: pretrained decoders suffice for tabular RL, but block-MDP lower bounds yield exponential sample separation. Structured exogenous noise degrades temporal contrastive learning more than forward modeling; iid Gaussian noise favors temporal contrastive; trajectory-based ACRO remains robust.
  - 社区 C0016 的组织线索：Four RL works on distinct topics: video representation learning, learned optimizers via environment design, path-tracing sampling/denoising, and strategic option generation.


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.

I found the five papers matching this toolkit. Here they are, with a comparison of their experimental results.

## (a) Anchor-free one-stage part-whole human detection
**PBADet (ICLR 2024)** — D0063. One-stage anchor-free extension of YOLOv5/YOLOv7 with a single part-to-body center offset.
- **COCOHumanParts (all categories AP .5:.95):** YOLOv7 = 42.7/41.5; YOLOv5l6 = 43.0/41.8.
- **BodyHands:** anchor-free part-to-body (Joint AP 85.98) beats anchor-based part-to-body (85.28) and BPJDet body-to-part (78.13), with fewer params (36.9M vs 41.2M).
- **CrowdHuman (face-body):** Ours-YOLOv7 MR⁻² 36.5/44.7, AP 91.6/81.6 — best MR⁻² among one-stage methods; ablations show the association head, multi-scale offset, and task-alignment each improve Joint AP.

**N原judge：** The generated answer accurately captures the core findings and experimental results across all five papers, consistent with the gold answers and adding only compatible supporting details.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**(a) PBADet (D0063)** — On **COCOHumanParts**, Ours(YOLOv5l6) gives AP.5:.95 = 43.0/41.8 (orig/subordinate), AP.5 = 70.0/68.4, AP_M = 66.2, AP_L = 67.2, on par with BPJDet (43.6/43.3, 70.6/69.8, 63.8, 61.8) while leading on AP_M/AP_L and person/feet categories. On **BodyHands**, the anchor-free part-to-body variant clearly beats anchor-based BPJDet: HandAP 89.1 vs 85.3, Cond. Accuracy 92.62 vs 86.80, JointAP 85.98 vs 78.13. On **CrowdHuman** face-body, Ours(YOLOv7) reaches lower MR⁻² (36.5/44.7 body/face) and higher body AP (91.6) than BPJDet. Ablations show task-alignment and multi-scale offsets each boost JointAP (78.07 → 85.98).

## Cross-cutting analysis
- **Common thread:** squared-error/latent-space objectives + standard stochastic optimizers suffice for all five; the papers are complementary — (d) makes training memory-lean for the Transformers used in (c)/(e), (b)/(c) provide theory (spectral/implicit-bias) explaining *why* the objectives work, (a) provides a scalable one-stage benchmark-scale detector, and (e) supplies RL-specific theory.
- **Where each "wins":** PBADet wins on association accuracy/efficiency vs two-stage/anchor baselines; DANN-RNN beats ColEI on accuracy, with NSE as the diagnostic; JEPA beats MAE on noisy-feature filtering; 4-bit AdamW ≈ full precisio…

## 1. Latent prediction vs reconstruction; contrastive vs forward strategies
**Read D0048 (“JEPA and MAE feature learning dynamics”) + D0003 (“Video-based representation learning for RL”).**

- D0048: On high-dimensional deep linear models, JEPA (latent prediction) and MAE (reconstruction) share SVD dynamics, but JEPA is implicitly biased toward **influential features** (high regression coefficients), while MAE prioritizes highly-covarying features even if noisy. JEPA’s bias only holds when the encoder is deep; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. On ImageNet ViT, JEPA learns low-variance features faster and often achieves better downstream classification with fewer steps — i.e., latent prediction beats reconstruction for perception when the encoder is deep.
- D0003: In video pretraining for RL, **forward modeling and temporal contrastive** both provably recover the latent state with polynomial sample complexity under iid noise only. Under **exogenous (temporally-correlated) noise**, temporal contrastive completely fails (it can overfit the predictable noise), forward modeling is more robust but degrades as noise grows, and trajectory-based ACRO is best. Autoencoding has no finite-sample guarantee but performs empirically well on ViZDoom. Practical takeaway: prefer forward/lat…

**D0003 – "Towards Principled Representation Learning from Videos for RL" (ICLR 2024)**
Compares exactly the three strategies you ask about for **unlabeled video pretraining → RL**: autoencoder (reconstruction), forward modeling (predicting future observations = latent prediction), and temporal contrastive learning.
- **Theory:** With only iid observation noise, forward modeling and temporal contrastive provably recover the latent MDP state and give polynomial-sample downstream RL; no guarantee exists for autoencoders. With **exogenous (temporally correlated) noise**, video pretraining is *exponentially harder* than action-labeled trajectory data (lower bound).
- **Empirics (GridWorld, ViZDoom):** Without exogenous noise, both forward and contrastive succeed. With exogenous noise, **temporal contrastive completely fails** (it cheats by tracking predictable noise), **forward modeling degrades but stays robust** (it must predict future observations, so state info remains useful), and the autoencoder works well in ViZDoom but not GridWorld. Trajectory-based ACRO is the strong…

### 1. Part–body association — PBADet (D0063)
One-stage, anchor-free detector using a single part-to-body center offset. On **BodyHands** (hand-body), PBADet(YOLOv7, 36.9M params) achieves **HandAP 89.1 / Cond. Accuracy 92.62 / JointAP 85.98**, beating BPJDet(YOLOv5m6) (85.3/86.80/78.13) with a smaller model; on **COCOHumanParts** it is on par with BPJDet (AP.5:.95 42.7 vs 43.6) but leads in per-person/feet AP and lowest mMR−2. Ablations isolate each design choice: the association loss raises Cond. Acc from 80.78→92.62; anchor-free part-to-body (85.98) > anchor-based part-to-body (85.28) > anchor-based body-to-part BPJDet (78.13) on JointAP. Against ED-Pose (Swin-L) on COCO parts, PBADet yields much higher **Precision 39.4 vs 24.1, Recall 63.1 vs 45.5, F1 48.5 vs 31.5** — direct CE/Precision/F1 evidence that anchor-free part-to-body association is more reliable than multi-person-pose limb prediction.

Flip-signal online updates eliminate latent weights: weight storage drops to O(n²L/32) vs O(n²L) for BPTT/OTTT; training memory is **constant (~2.9/3.1 GB) as timesteps grow, vs BPTT rising 2.86→58.18 GB (20.3×)**. **C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## 1. Anchor-free part–body association — PBADet (D0063)
- **BodyHands:** Ours(YOLOv7, 36.9M params) achieves **HandAP 89.1, Cond. Accuracy 92.62, JointAP 85.98**, beating BPJDet-YOLOv5m6 (85.3/86.80/78.13, 41.2M) and BodyHands (84.8/84.12/63.87, 700.3M) with a far smaller model.
- **Ablation:** the association head/loss is what drives association quality: removing it keeps HandAP at 89.1 but collapses Cond. Acc. 92.62→80.78 and JointAP 85.98→78.07.
- **COCOHumanParts:** Ours matches BPJDet in AP.5:.95 (42.7/41.5 vs 43.6/43.3) but **leads in AP_M/AP_L for person and feet** and attains the **lowest mMR−2** on head, face, both hands and right foot. Anchor-free part-to-body (89.1/92.62/85.98) beats anchor-based part-to-body (88.4/92.31/85.28) and BPJDet's anchor-based body-to-part (85.3/86.80/78.13).
- **Analysis:** the single part→body center offset gives one-to-one association that stays valid under occlusion (body-to-part offsets become invalid), which is why it scales to 6 parts without degrading detection.

## 2. Online training for binary/spiking nets — BSO/T-BSO (D0035)
- **CIFAR-10:** T-BSO **94.86%** (4 steps), 94.70% (6), 94.32% (2) with a model **30.8× smaller** than FP-SNN (93.23%); +0.97% over OTTT.
- **CIFAR-100:** T-BSO **74.27%** (6), 73.82% (4), 73.40% (2) — +0.79% …

<details>
<summary>原问题</summary>

I’m building an edge‑constrained system that needs: (a) reliable hand/face‑to‑person association in crowded images at COCO scale; (b) label‑free pretraining that predicts one view’s representation from another instead of reconstructing pixels; (c) a recurrent controller that respects separate excitatory vs inhibitory units yet still trains well; (d) a policy learner that can start from a static log and keep improving with on‑policy updates while retaining theoretical stability; and (e) the ability to fine‑tune Transformer backbones/LLMs under tight VRAM using ~4‑bit AdamW states. Are there recent papers that collectively address these components, with experiments spanning COCO, CIFAR‑100/MNIST/PTB and common fine‑tuning setups?Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

</details>


| 指标 | N naive | C fallback community |
|---|---:|---:|
| QA token（含embedding） | 465,739 | 286,620 |
| QA实际耗时/秒 | 155.55 | 146.42 |
| 评分 | 4 | 3 |


**差异原因：数值与对象核验。** C 少两轮后把 HNPG 的纯 on-policy baseline TRPO 写成 PPO，且夸大 COCOHumanParts AP；五篇均在。需要防止被同社区相近算法名干扰，但现有 trace 不能证明错误名字具体来自哪段社区文本。


**社区信息的具体作用。** 本题累计展示 15 个社区、61 篇成员文档，其中 5 篇在参考文档集合 G 中，56 篇不在 G 中。去掉本题曾返回原始 chunk 的文档，仍有 **42 篇仅通过社区提供 overview**（其中参考文档 0 篇）。这部分才是纯原文检索之外的背景增量；不在 G 中不自动等于无关。

C 没有补入 N 完全未见的参考文档。社区仍可能提供组织线索、相邻方法或更早提示，但本题的评分差不能解释为“终于找到了新的必需论文”。

没有“先由社区看到参考文档、再明确按该 doc_id 获取原文”的新文档导航链。后续动作主要是继续验证已知论文或自由搜索。

未发现仅由社区overview提供的文档在最终答案中的显式ID引用或已记录的独有短语联系。因此本题不能把背景存在直接称为“答案使用了社区知识”。

|---|---|---|---|
| D0030 Hybrid RL: Using an Offline Dataset to Interleave Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning | C0040 Reinforcement Learning: Data, Dynamics, and Transfer | 1 / 1 | 是 |
| D0048 JEPA and MAE Feature Learning Dynamics: High-Dimensional Linear Models and Critical Times | C0023 Self-Supervised Learning Theory & Methods | 1 / 1 | 是 |

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0030：Presents hybrid RL algorithms HAC and HNPG combining offline data with on-policy natural policy gradient. They achieve best-of-both-worlds suboptimality and sample-complexity guarantees under approximate Bellman completeness. Experiments show HNPG solving continuous and image-based combination locks where TRPO/RLPD fail.
  - 社区 C0040 的组织线索：Four RL papers: offline-to-online policy optimization, active exploration for sim-to-real manipulation, cross-domain dynamics filtering, and random-feature model-free planning.


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


这些概览能够帮助找到方法和实验方向，但通常没有同一表中的 baseline/数据集/指标/配置四元组。数值或胜负变化应归到实际表格证据和答案取舍，不能仅归到社区名字。

I’m interested in links to regularization under cross-entropy, practical optimizer choices, and how to keep GPU memory low during training.Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0069：Column-constrained excitatory-inhibitory (ColEI) RNNs obeying Dale’s Law learn worse than standard RNNs and DANNs.   - 社区 C0041 的组织线索：These three object detection papers: PBADet for human part-body association, HASSOD for class-agnostic object discovery, and MonoUNI for monocular 3D detection.

## Cross-method analysis
- **Complementarity:** D0014 tells you how small-batch contrastive pretraining degrades representations (negative-pair variance) and offers a loss fix; D0048 explains why a JEPA-style objective may give more discriminative (high-influence) features for downstream identity matching than reconstruction. PBADet handles the actual hand/face→person matching at inference in crowded scenes, one-stage and anchor-free, with strong gains over BPJDet (especially hand association accuracy, ~6 points) and over anchor-based backbones at equal parameters. D0059 reduces the memory bottleneck of fine-tuning the transf…

| **Ours (YOLOv7)** | **36.9M** | **1024** | **89.1** | **92.62** | **85.98** |

PBADet beats all baselines with ~2.3× fewer params and 512-px-lower input resolution. On COCOHumanParts it matches BPJDet while leading AP_M/AP_L and giving the lowest average mMR−2 (mismatch rate) for head/face/both hands; on CrowdHuman it improves body MR−2 (36.5 vs 40.7) and body AP (91.6 vs 89.5) over BPJDet. Ablations show the association head adds ~7.9 points of joint AP (78.07→85.98) with zero detection cost (HandAP unchanged 89.1), and anchor-free part-to-body beats anchor-based body-to-part (JointAP 85.98 vs 78.13). *This is the tight-compute anchor-free method you asked for.*

**(b) AMP — D0041** (adaptive message passing)
- Variationally learns depth + per-layer message filtering; mitigates oversmoothing (Dirichlet energy does not decay exponentially), oversquashing (learned filtering reduces messages), underreaching (learned depth).
- Competitive with SOTA on five node/graph prediction sets (synthetic long-range tasks, peptides-func, peptides-struct, node classification); learns very deep architectures only when needed; can drastically cut propagated information vs classical message passing.

**(c) JEPA implicit bias — D0048** (self-distillation, latent-space prediction)
- JEPA biased toward "influential" features (large regression coefficients), unlike MAE's pixel-space MSE; bias holds only for deep encoders (1-layer JEPA = infinite-depth MAE).
- ImageNet ViT: I-JEPA learns the low-variance (bottom-25%-explained-variance, perceptual) subspace faster than MAE — higher CCA between full and "bottom" features, reversed for "top"; noisy features learned later/lower amplitude.

Normalised SVD entropy measures this pathology and anti-correlates with test error.

  - 社区 C0021 的组织线索：Five papers on graph neural networks: edge embeddings, expressivity/counting, adaptive message passing, world models, and continual domain adaptation.

**2. Graph – long-range without oversmoothing/oversquashing (D0041, AMP, ICML 2025)**
- Variational framework that learns message-passing depth and per-layer soft message filtering; linear complexity O(|V|), fully differentiable.
- Results: on synthetic long-range tasks (Diameter/SSSP/Eccentricity) AMP cuts test error on average by 63%/72%/32% over base GCN/GIN/ADGN; on peptides-func it improves AP by 2–3.4% over base models (AMPGCN 0.7161) and reaches state-of-the-art MAE on peptides-struct (0.2446), competing with rewiring/transformer baselines (Exphormer, GRIT, GPS). The paper shows Dirichlet energy does not decay exponentially (oversmoothing mitigated) and sensitivity upper bound is reduced (oversquashing mitigated); metrics: log10(MSE), AP, MAE.

Finally, our control stack uses recurrent modules with excitatory/inhibitory sign constraints inspired by biology, so I need guidance on spectral conditions for stable training. Are there works that address these needs together and report results on standard image datasets before deployment?Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

### 2. Hyper-parameter search without hyper-gradients (D0056 — Cubic-Regularized Stochastic Relaxation)
Matches your need: no hyper-gradients (works for non-differentiable F1/Precision metrics and discrete hyper-parameters), and uses **curvature beyond quadratic penalties** — it obtains gradient + Hessian via stochastic relaxation and uses **cubic regularization** to escape saddle points, converging to second-order stationary points. Results:
- Synthetic mask learning: beats gradient/natural-gradient/Newton relaxations on validation AUC, and is the only method whose found optimum has non-dominant negative Hessian eigenvalues (saddle escape).
- Knowledge-graph completion (FB15k237, WN18RR): faster convergence and higher MRR than Random/BO/Hyperband/RL.
- **Noisy-label CIFAR-10 schedule search (50% symmetric, 45% pair-flip):** more sample-efficient and converges to a more accurate model (image data ✓). Ablations: more Hessian samples K and more training epochs both help, unless wall-clock limited.

### 5. The actual vision deployment task (D0063 — PBADet)
No corpus work covers a robot that must label hands as technician vs. patient specifically, but PBADet addresses the closest task — **detecting hands and associating each hand to its correct body in crowded scenes**, and it explic…

**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**2. Hyper-parameter search without hyper-gradients, using curvature — D0056 (cubic-regularized stochastic relaxation).**
Matches exactly: obtains gradient + Hessian of the relaxed objective *without* hyper-gradients, and cubic regularization (beyond quadratic penalties) escapes saddle points, converging to approximate second-order stationary points. Experimental results:
- Knowledge-graph HPO (FB15k237, WN18RR, discrete HPs): higher MRR and faster convergence than Random/BO/Hyperband/RL, closer to global optimum.
- Noisy-label CIFAR-10 schedule search (50% symmetric, 45% pair-flip): more efficient and converges to a more accurate model than baselines; larger K (gradient/Hessian samples) and more epochs improve results.

**Conclusion.** Adopt the stack piecewise: D0059 (4-bit AdamW/SGD) for the GPU budget, D0056 (cubic-regularized HPO) for non-differentiable F1/Precision criteria, D0048's mechanism to justify JEPA pretraining, D0069's spectral/NSE guidance (DANN-style EI, gradient clipping) for the recurrent control stack, and D0063 as the closest prior art for hand–person association — but be aware that no retrieved work evaluates the combined system, or reports F1/Precision on a hospital deployment dataset.

**C原judge：** The generated answer correctly captures the main cubic-regularization hyperparameter-optimization results and ablations, but it omits some key experimental details from the gold standard such as the synthetic GD/NG/Newton comparison, eigenvalue saddle-point analysis, and the time-cost finding.

Based on the retrieved documents, here is the paper set covering all five pieces, with experimental results:

## (d) Small recurrent control loop with E/I separation, still trainable → **Dale's Law RNNs** (D0069)
"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" studies RNNs respecting excitatory/inhibitory separation (Dale's law): ColEI (partitioned units) vs DANN (reparameterized E-to-E/E-to-I/I-to-E, extendable recurrently).
- **Results:** Naive ColEI partitioning impairs learning (multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectra); recurrent DANNs learn as well as standard RNNs while respecting E/I separation, robust even with 1 inhibitory neuron (sequential MNIST experiments). Spectrum, not sign constraints, drives performance; normalized SVD entropy predicts learning. → Use recurrent DANN-style E/I parameterization for a trainable, Dale's-law-compliant control loop.

**N原judge：** The generated answer accurately matches the gold answer by covering all five requested components with the correct papers and consistent experimental results, and any additional details or minor wording differences do not contradict the gold content.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**(d) Small recurrent control loop with E/I separation, still trainable → "Learning better with Dale's Law" (D0069)**
Compares column-constrained excitatory/inhibitory (ColEI) RNNs vs. recurrent Dale's-ANNs (DANN) vs. standard RNNs on adding, sequential MNIST, PTB, object recognition. (Optionally BSO, D0035, for online binary-spiking training with near-constant memory.)

**(d)** ColEI (the naive E/I column constraint) learns worse and more variably across all four tasks; recurrent DANNs — which respect Dale's Law but use W = W_EE·W_EI·W_IE with non-negative blocks — learn as well as standard RNNs and stay robust even with one inhibitory unit. Spectrum transplants show the singular-value spectrum (multimodal in ColEI), not the sign constraint, determines performance; normalized SVD entropy predicts test error. So for a *trainable* E/I loop, use the recurrent DANN formulation, not ColEI.

**C原judge：** The generated answer correctly identifies the five core papers and accurately summarizes most of their experimental findings, but it omits the cross-paper MMLU comparison and includes a questionable DANN weight formula, so it is not perfect.

**5. Practical multi-person detection (D0063 + D0015)**

## LoRA fine-tuning tips
- **D0060**: LoRA fine-tuning improves task performance but does **not** produce the power-law Hessian structure that full-parameter fine-tuning creates — suggesting full-parameter and LoRA fine-tuning may have different generalization abilities; for pretrained models the Hessian trace Tr(H) is a more reliable generalization indicator than spectral distance.
- **D0029 GOT-D** and **D0032 NFTS**: relevant fine-tuning strategies — GOT-D for selecting unlabeled data for two-stage/pre-fine-tuning (up to +13.9% AGNews at 40k), and NFTS for searching which layers to fine-tune or insert adapters in few-shot settings.

**Key comparisons across methods:** PBADet shows a single-offset anchor-free design is more parameter-efficient and accurate than multi-offset/body-to-part methods (precision/conditional-accuracy improvements of ~6 pts). JEPA-vs-MAE (D0048) and NSE (D0069) both show that *spectral/latent structure* — not raw sign or pixel constraints — drives learnability. 4-bit optimizers (D0059) achieve near-lossless accuracy with a large memory reduction, complementing LoRA's low-rank parameter counts. GenMS (D0026) demonstrates that pure LLM generation fails (~0% validity/match), while hierarchical LLM+diffusion+GNN succeeds (>80% instruction following), which …

**N原judge：** The generated answer correctly identifies all five core papers and provides generally accurate experimental comparisons, but it omits the gold answer's specific end-to-end LoRA fine-tuning heuristics (4-bit quantization choices, FSDP/fused-kernel use) and contains a few imprecise numeric/qualitative claims, so it is good but not perfect.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**LoRA fine-tuning tips:** **D0060** — during LoRA fine-tuning of TinyLlama-1B on MathQA, the power-law Hessian structure of the adapters forms after ~500 steps; λ₁ rises then Hessian trace Tr(H) consistently decreases, making **Tr(H) a more reliable generalization indicator** than sharpness for pretrained models (KS distance of the power-law fit also correlates with test loss, Pearson ~0.98). Note that LoRA improves task performance but does not reshape full-parameter Hessian structure the way full fine-tuning does. Related fine-tuning tips: **D0001 (NEFTune)** adds noise to embeddings during instruction fine-tuning (AlpacaEval 29.8%→64.7%, gains plateau after ~3 epochs, frozen attention blocks remove the gains); **D0071 (PCP)** shows prompt-templated continued pre-training before prompt-based fine-tuning helps (up to +20.1% absolute) while naive continued pre-training can hurt sentence-pair tasks; **D0029 (GOT-D)** selects unlabeled data for a pre-fine-tuning stage before targeted fine-tuning (e.g., +13.9% AGNews at 40k).

## Cross-method comparison
- **Common theme:** every method trades memory/complexity for accuracy and validates against full-precision/full-parameter counterparts — PBADet keeps detection AP while adding association; 4-bit AdamW is lossless vs 32-bit; JEPA tr…

**C原judge：** The generated answer accurately identifies and summarizes all five requested methods—JEPA, PBADet, GenMS, 4-bit Adam/AdamW, and Dale's-law RNN diagnostics—with correct experimental comparisons and only consistent supplementary context, so it fully matches the gold answers.


</details>

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


- D0015：DiffusionFake is a plug-and-play framework that improves cross-domain deepfake detection by reversing forgery generation with frozen Stable Diffusion. It injects detector features to reconstruct source/target images. Trained on FF++, it raises AUC (EfficientNet-B4 75.80→81.88; ViT-B 77.44→83.78). Requires paired images; no error bars; code planned.
  - 社区 C0029 的组织线索：Covers diffusion-model guidance, deepfake detection, and adversarial image attacks, plus a black-box attack on image-to-text models.


这些概览能够帮助找到方法和实验方向，但通常没有同一表中的 baseline/数据集/指标/配置四元组。数值或胜负变化应归到实际表格证据和答案取舍，不能仅归到社区名字。

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


- D0059：Proposes 4-bit quantization of Adam/AdamW states via normalization and dynamic exponent mapping, with block-wise or rank-1 normalization for outliers. Second moment uses zero-excluding mapping and rank-1 scaling. Matches full-precision across GLUE, E2E, SQuAD, Swin, LLaMA; up to 57.7% memory savings. Provides convergence theorem for quantized SGD.
  - 社区 C0027 的组织线索：Efficient neural network optimization: online binary spiking training, quantized 4-bit optimizer states, and compressed distributed SGD, all with convergence guarantees.

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


- D0059：Proposes 4-bit quantization of Adam/AdamW states via normalization and dynamic exponent mapping, with block-wise or rank-1 normalization for outliers. Second moment uses zero-excluding mapping and rank-1 scaling. Matches full-precision across GLUE, E2E, SQuAD, Swin, LLaMA; up to 57.7% memory savings. Provides convergence theorem for quantized SGD.
  - 社区 C0027 的组织线索：Efficient neural network optimization: online binary spiking training, quantized 4-bit optimizer states, and compressed distributed SGD, all with convergence guarantees.

Yes — the collection contains works covering each need. Here is the comparison by topic.

## 6. SGD/AdamW settings, attention/embedding design, Precision/F1 evaluation
- **Optimizer settings**: D0059 (above); D0060 compares SGD vs AdamW across models — SGD underperforms Adam for Transformers when Hessian spectra show blockwise heterogeneity; AdamW with LR 6e-4, weight decay 0.1, warmup for LLMs.
- **Attention/embedding design**: D0061 details SSL design (projector 8192-8192-512 / 4096-256, LARS/cosine, batch scaling); D0015 (DiffusionFake) uses channel/spatial attention + multi-head cross-attention in a feature-filter module with disentangled source/target embeddings, raising deepfake AUC (EfficientNet-B4 75.80→81.88; ViT-B 77.44→83.78).
- **Precision/F1**: D0016 defines F1 = 2·Recall·Precision/(Recall+Precision); D0029 reports F1 (macro/micro) for fine-tuning evaluation; D0063 uses AP/mMR−2; D0061 reports AP (object detection/segmentation) and accuracy.

**N原judge：** The generated answer correctly covers all five requested topics with appropriate comparisons and extra context, but it is not perfect because it misreports PBADet's BodyHands metrics (swapping hand AP and conditional accuracy) and includes some unverified numerical details.


**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**1. Hand/face detection for gesture UI on a resource-constrained robot — PBADet (D0063).** One-stage anchor-free part-body association detecting body, left/right hands, and face with a single part-to-body center offset (smaller representation than BPJDet: 10 vs 15). Practical settings: PyTorch, SGD (same schedule as YOLOv7), AMP, 4×V100, 100 epochs. Results: on BodyHands, hand AP 89.1 / cond. accuracy 92.62 / joint AP 85.98 vs BPJDet's 85.3–85.9 / 86.91 / 84.39; on CrowdHuman, body MR⁻² 36.5 vs 40.7 (BPJDet). vs ED-Pose it reports Precision/Recall/F1: all-parts F1 48.52 vs 31.51, and hand F1 ~46.5–47.3 vs ~22.9–24.2. It also matches/leads on COCOHumanParts AP.

**Cross-method takeaways:** D0063 is the strongest match for detection (Precision/F1 + AP, SGD settings included); D0059/D0060 give the tightest SGD/AdamW guidance for low-memory Transformer fine-tuning (F1 used for QA); D0048 supports JEPA-style MSE self-distillation over reconstruction for perception pretraining; D0069 supplies the spectral diagnostic (NSE) for E/I RNN stability; D0066/D0052 address budget-limited sim→real transfer, D0066 via value-target source-data filtering exactly as requested.

**C原judge：** The generated answer covers all five requested areas and most key experimental results accurately, but it has minor factual inaccuracies (e.g., GPT-2 LR 6e-4 vs gold's 4e-5) and slight overstatements, so it is good but not perfect.

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.


- D0059：Proposes 4-bit quantization of Adam/AdamW states via normalization and dynamic exponent mapping, with block-wise or rank-1 normalization for outliers. Second moment uses zero-excluding mapping and rank-1 scaling. Matches full-precision across GLUE, E2E, SQuAD, Swin, LLaMA; up to 57.7% memory savings. Provides convergence theorem for quantized SGD.
  - 社区 C0027 的组织线索：Efficient neural network optimization: online binary spiking training, quantized 4-bit optimizer states, and compressed distributed SGD, all with convergence guarantees.


这些概览能够帮助找到方法和实验方向，但通常没有同一表中的 baseline/数据集/指标/配置四元组。数值或胜负变化应归到实际表格证据和答案取舍，不能仅归到社区名字。

Here is research that maps to each of your five needs, with a comparison of their experimental results.

## 1. Real-time path tracing (<30 ms) with adaptive sampling → D0082
"RL-based Stateful Neural Adaptive Sampling and Denoising for Real-Time Path Tracing" (NeurIPS 2023)
- Trains three networks (sampling-importance U-Net, latent-space encoder CNN, denoiser U-Net) end-to-end; the sampler is trained with RL (APPO) instead of the numerically approximated gradient used by prior work.
- **Results:** 28.7 dB PSNR at 4.0 spp / **22.5 ms** (within your 30 ms budget); "ours-small" reaches 27.3 dB / 14.4 ms and is Pareto-optimal below ~38 ms.
- **Analysis/ablation:** RL beats the gradient-approximation variant by 0.3 dB; adaptive vs uniform sampling gains 0.8 dB; the latent-space encoder adds 0.7 dB; keeping individual sample values instead of averages adds 0.5 dB. A 2 spp budget still outperforms every baseline at 4 spp (0.2 dB higher at 1.6× lower latency). Notably, this paper also replaces an *explicit numerically approximated gradient* with an implicit learned one — directly relevant to your "practical approximations in place of exact gradients" theme (see also §5).

**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

Here are the matching works and a comparison of their experimental results:

## 1. Real-time path tracing (D0082) — RL-based adaptive sampling & denoising
- **Results:** Reaches **28.7 dB PSNR at 4.0 spp in 22.5 ms/frame** (<30 ms budget). Outperforms prior adaptive-sampling SOTA NTAS (27.7 dB @ 17.4 ms) by ~1 dB at slightly higher latency; beats DASR (27.2 dB), IMCD (27.9 dB @ 46.4 ms), ReSTIR+OIDN (28.0 dB @ 18.3 ms).
- **Ablations:** RL-based sampling beats gradient approximation by +0.3 dB; adaptive beats uniform by +0.8 dB; latent-space encoder + temporal feedback adds +0.7–1.3 dB; keeping individual samples vs. averages adds +0.5 dB. A smaller variant ("ours-small", 27.3 dB @ 14.4 ms) is Pareto-optimal up to 38 ms.
- **Analysis:** Uses RL (APPO) instead of numerically approximated gradients — relevant to your "practical approximations in place of exact gradients" idea. Memory overhead is ~200 MB total, so it coexists with tight GPU budgets, but requires dedicated DNN + ray-tracing capacity.

**C原judge：** The generated answer comprehensively matches the gold comparison across all five areas, but it has a minor numerical imprecision (e.g., listing BPJDet's BodyHands Hand AP as 86.1 instead of 85.9), so it is not perfect.

## 2. Recurrent models under Dale's law (D0069)
ColEI RNNs (column-wise E/I sign constraints) train poorly. Using spectral tools, the paper shows the **singular-value spectrum at initialization matters more than the sign constraints**: ColEI spectra are multimodal/dispersed while DANN and standard RNNs are unimodal (Marchenko–Pastur). **Results (sequential MNIST):** sign constraints alone hurt by only 0.7±0.3% (RNN) and 1±1% (ColEI), but the full ColEI–RNN gap is 2.3±0.6%; spectrum "transplants" reproduce most of the gap (1.5±0.3% / 2±1%), exceeding sign-constraint effects. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) anti-correlates with final test error across sizes/EI ratios; ColEIs are highly unstable without gradient clipping (explaining training instability).

## 4. 4-bit memory-saving optimizers (D0059)
Quantizes first/second moments to 4-bit via smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, and a zero-point-excluding linear quantizer for the second moment (with optional factorization). **Results:** matches full-precision fine-tuning on GLUE (NLU 89.1 vs 88.9), Swin ImageNet (80.8 vs 81.2), E2E BLEU (67.8 vs 67.7), SQuAD (94.5 vs 94.6), WMT14 (26.28 vs 26.61); LLaMA-7B MMLU 38.9 vs 38.7, with closely aligned convergence. Saves up to **57.7% memory** (LLaMA-7B: 31.87 GB vs 75.40 GB), even outperfo…

## 2. Dale's Law RNNs: A Spectral Perspective (D0069)
Analyzes E/I sign-constrained RNNs (ColEI vs DANN) on adding problem, sequential MNIST, PTB, naturalistic object recognition, using SVD/normalized-SVD-entropy (NSE).
- ColEI learns worst on all four tasks and is far more variable across seeds; gradient clipping helps it substantially (instability).
- **Key finding:** the *singular-value spectrum*, not sign constraints, drives the gap. Sign constraints cost only ~0.7–1%, whereas the full ColEI-vs-RNN gap is 2.3%±0.6%; spectrum "transplants" contribute more (RNNs 1.5%±0.3%, ColEI 2%±1%). ColEI's multimodal/dispersed spectrum (with a large-singular-value mode) explains exploding/vanishing directions and instability, while DANN RNNs (unimodal spectrum, matching random-matrix theory) learn as well as standard RNNs.
- NSE at initialization anti-correlates with final test error: small balanced-E/I nets (high NSE) outperform large skewed nets (low NSE).

## Cross-method analysis
- **Direct numeric comparison is not meaningful** — the works target disjoint benchmarks (symbolic/arithmetic LLM tasks, RNN time-series/MNIST, SSL theory, optimizer memory on GLUE/ImageNet/LLaMA, detection AP on BodyHands/COCOHumanParts). Only item (2) reports sequential MNIST; none reports CIFAR interpretabi…

## 1. Anchor-free part–whole association — PBADet (D0063)
One-stage anchor-free detector using a single 2D part-to-body center offset (part→body, vs BPJDet's body→part). Trained with **SGD**, 1024×1024 input, 4×V100, 100 epochs.
- **BodyHands:** Ours(YOLOv7, 36.9M) → HandAP 89.1, Cond-Acc 92.62, JointAP 85.98 vs BPJDet(YOLOv5m6, 41.2M, 1536px) 85.3/86.80/78.13 and BPJDet(YOLOv5l6, 86.1M) 85.9/86.91/84.39 — better with **fewer params and lower resolution**.
- **Ablations (Table 8):** anchor-free part-to-body (89.1/92.62/85.98) > anchor-based part-to-body (88.4/92.31/85.28) > BPJDet anchor-based body-to-part (85.3/86.80/78.13). Association head adds almost no detection cost but jumps Cond-Acc 80.78→92.62 (Table 4).
- **COCOHumanParts:** AP.5:.95 43.0/41.8 ≈ BPJDet (43.6/43.3), but leads AP_M, AP_L and feet; lowest mMR−2 for head/face/hands.
- **Fit:** ideal for crowded-scene HCI under memory limits; the 2D-offset representation is the cheapest association mechanism among those compared.

## 2. Compiled attention for exact arithmetic — Neural Comprehension (D0010)
CoNNs (transformer modules with hand-compiled attention weights) gated into LMs; fully neural, end-to-end differentiable, no external tools.
- **Symbolic tasks:** ~100% flawless on parity/reverse/add/subtract with perfect …

Based on the retrieved papers, here is a comparative analysis of the experimental results for each of your five needs:

## 1. Anchor-free part–whole association — PBADet (D0063)
On **BodyHands**, PBADet (YOLOv7, 36.9M params, 1024 input) beats all prior work: **HandAP 89.1, Cond. Accuracy 92.62, JointAP 85.98** vs. BPJDet(YOLOv5l6) 85.9/86.91/84.39 and BodyHands 84.8/83.44/63.48. Ablations isolate the design: removing the association loss collapses Cond. Acc. from 92.62→80.78 and JointAP 85.98→78.07; dropping multi-scale (91.64/85.46) or task-alignment (92.08/85.78) also hurts. The anchor-free **part-to-body** offset beats its own anchor-based variant (89.1 vs 88.4 HandAP) and BPJDet's anchor-based body-to-part (85.3). On **COCOHumanParts** it matches BPJDet on AP.5:.95 (43.0 vs 43.6) but leads on medium/large AP (66.2/67.2 vs 63.8/61.8) and has the lowest mMR−2 on head/face/hands/right-foot. **Verdict:** one-stage, anchor-free, lower memory (1024 vs 1536 input, fewer params) while improving or matching accuracy — good fit for edge HCI.

**C原judge：** The generated answer is largely accurate and comprehensive, but it contains a minor factual contradiction (claiming lowest mMR−2 on right-foot whereas the gold reports worse right-foot) and omits key cross-paper comparisons such as the GSM8K results, so it is not perfect but is clearly correct overall.

**N答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

**2. Spectral perspective on Dale's-Law RNNs — D0069 ("Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective", NeurIPS 2023)**
Shows that the poor learning of sign-constrained (excitatory/inhibitory) RNNs is caused mainly by the **singular-value spectrum at initialization**, not the sign constraints. Column-constrained (ColEI) RNNs have multimodal, dispersed spectra (rank-one nilpotent column-mean matrix), whereas standard RNNs and DANN RNNs follow the Marchenko–Pastur quarter-circle. Proposes **normalized SVD entropy (NSE)** as a pre-training diagnostic. A complementary spectral/optimizer-dynamics analysis is **D0060 ("Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure")**, which studies power-law Hessian spectra (β≈1.8–2.3) under SGD/Adam/AMSGrad and uses Hessian eigengaps to explain robust low-dimensional learning subspaces and generalization.

**4. Memory-frugal 4-bit optimizer states — D0059 ("Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States", NeurIPS 2023)**
Pushes Adam/AdamW optimizer states to 4-bit via smaller block size, rank-1 (row+column) normalization, and a zero-point-excluding linear quantizer for the second moment; plus factorization (4-bitFactor). General framework covers SGDM, Adam, AdamW; includes a convergence theorem for quantized SGD.

**C答案片段**（按本case涉及的主题节选，完整答案见trace）：

## 1. One-stage anchor-free part-body association — **PBADet (D0063)**
Extends anchor-free detection with a single part-to-body center offset. **Results:** on BodyHands it beats the anchor-based BPJDet (hand AP 89.1 vs 85.3; cond. accuracy 92.62 vs 86.80; joint AP 85.98 vs 78.13); on COCOHumanParts it matches/exceeds it (AP 42.7–43.0); on CrowdHuman face-body it lowers MR−2 (36.5/44.7 vs 40.7/46.3) and generalizes to quadruped animals. Ablations show anchor-free > anchor-based and part-to-body > body-to-part, and task-alignment learning is essential. *Themes: attention-free, interpretable association, efficient single-stage design.*

## 2. Spectral view of Dale's Law RNNs — **Learning better with Dale's Law (D0069)**
Analyzes RNNs with excitatory/inhibitory sign constraints (ColEI vs DANN). **Results:** ColEI RNNs learn worse and more variably on adding, sequential MNIST, Penn TreeBank, and natural object recognition. Spectrum-transplant experiments show the singular-value spectrum (multimodal/dispersed for ColEI) matters more than sign constraints for learning; normalized SVD entropy (NSE) at initialization anti-correlates with final test error and predicts performance. **Caveat for your query:** training uses (projected) gradient descent, not explicitly SGD/AdamW, so the SGD/Ad…

Yes — five separate works cover your five needs (no single paper addresses all combined). Comparing their experimental results:

**1. Part–body association (PBADet, D0063).** One-stage, anchor-free with a single part-to-body center offset for body, face, left/right hands, left/right feet. On BodyHands: **HandAP 89.1, Conditional Accuracy 92.62, JointAP 85.98** (YOLOv7, 36.9M params) vs. BPJDet's 85.3/86.80/78.13 (41.2M) and 85.9/86.91/84.39 (86.1M) — it beats SOTA with a smaller model. On COCOHumanParts it is on par with BPJDet on all-category AP but leads on AP_M/AP_L and person/feet AP, and has the lowest mismatch rate (mMR-2) for head, face, both hands, and right foot. Ablations confirm anchor-free part-to-body > anchor-based part-to-body > BPJDet body-to-part (JointAP 85.98 vs 85.28 vs 78.13). This is the strongest match for your detector need.

**C原judge：** The answer comprehensively matches the gold answer on all major points, but includes a minor factual inaccuracy about PBADet achieving the lowest mismatch rate for the right foot on COCOHumanParts, where the gold numbers indicate BPJDet is lower.

<details>
<summary>原问题</summary>

I’m building a real-world system that needs: (1) a lightweight single-pass model to detect hands/face and link them to the correct person in crowded scenes; (2) a practical way to boost a transformer assistant’s instruction-following via a simple fine-tuning tweak on feature embeddings; (3) online, label-efficient calibration that guarantees low risk at every time step; and (4) guidance on designing recurrent controllers that respect excitatory/inhibitory constraints. I’d also like theory explaining why predicting in a learned representation space can avoid noisy cues in self-supervised pipelines. Are there works that collectively cover these needs?Please compare and analyze the experimental results of these methods.

**这些 overview 实际提供了什么：**


- D0063：PBADet introduces a one-stage, anchor-free detector for human part-body association, representing each part by a single 2D offset to its parent body center. It outperforms BPJDet on BodyHands, matches or exceeds it on COCOHumanParts, surpasses ED-Pose in part-body association, and generalizes to quadruped animal part-body association.
  - 社区 C0041 的组织线索：These three object detection papers: PBADet for human part-body association, HASSOD for class-agnostic object discovery, and MonoUNI for monocular 3D detection.


- D0048：Analyzes JEPA and MAE self-supervised learning in high-dimensional linear models. Both share SVD dynamics; 1-layer JEPA equals infinite-depth MAE. JEPA's critical time is variance-sensitive; MAE's leading term is variance-independent. Random masking and temporal covariance models diagonalize. ImageNet ViT: JEPA learns low-variance features faster.
  - 社区 C0023 的组织线索：Contrastive, masked, and joint-embedding SSL methods; embedding geometry, feature dynamics, and regularizers against collapse, plus a study of data selection under misspecification.
